title: Grateful Dead Live at Honolulu Civic Auditorium on 1970-01-23

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard recording of the Jan‑23‑1970 Hawaii show captures a high‑energy second half with standout jams on The Other One, Dark Star and Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The fixed‑Connor SBD is praised for its crystal‑clear mix and even lets the audience ambience shine through, making it one of the better early‑70 tapes. Musically the show is generally regarded as a top‑ten performance from that year – the long, fiery The Other One > Dark Star sequence, a scorching Lovelight and a soulful Black Peter dominate the praise, while a few listeners note a slightly flat‑lined first set. Overall the concert feels tight, trippy and historically significant.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 detailed reviews, most rating 4–5 stars, uniformly praise both the sound quality and the musical performance; only a few mixed comments keep the average just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clear and well‑balanced with good instrument isolation; audience bleed adds liveliness. A few notes mention minor pitch‑correction needs in the fixed file but no major dropouts or distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening, but the real fire erupts in the second half – China Cat > Rider transition kicks it off, followed by a marathon The Other One → Dark Star suite and an epic Lovelight that many call one of the best of ’70.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is highlighted as “perfect”, “majestically flowing” and featuring possibly his hottest slide work on tape.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal harmonies are praised (especially on Black Peter) and his Yellow Dog story/jokes get mention, plus he backs up Bobby on Mama Tried.
